title: Reduce-solve-transfer proves the Cubic Formula
intent: Prove the closed-form Cubic Formula by a reduce-solve-transfer composition: the glue rewrites the general cubic a*x^3 + b*x^2 + c*x + d = 0 into the depressed form y^3 + 3*p*y - 2*q = 0 through cubic_reduction, solves that depressed form with the three candidate roots s1, s2, s3 through cubic_basic (whose cube-root witness is supplied by ccbrt), then transfers the solution back to x through the same substitution.
also_known_as: reduce to a normal form, solve the normal form, transfer back through the reduction equivalence

parent.name: cubic
parent.statement:
lemma cubic:
  assumes a0: "a \<noteq> 0"
  shows
    "let
      p = (3 * a * c - b^2) / (9 * a^2);
      q = (9 * a * b * c - 2 * b^3 - 27 * a^2 * d) / (54 * a^3);
      s = csqrt(q^2 + p^3);
      s1 = (if p = 0 then ccbrt(2 * q) else ccbrt(q + s));
      s2 = -s1 * (1 + \<i> * csqrt 3) / 2;
      s3 = -s1 * (1 - \<i> * csqrt 3) / 2
     in
      if p = 0 then
        a * x^3 + b * x^2 + c * x + d = 0 \<longleftrightarrow>
          x = s1 - b / (3 * a) \<or>
          x = s2 - b / (3 * a) \<or>
          x = s3 - b / (3 * a)
      else
        s1 \<noteq> 0 \<and>
          (a * x^3 + b * x^2 + c * x + d = 0 \<longleftrightarrow>
            x = s1 - p / s1 - b / (3 * a) \<or>
            x = s2 - p / s2 - b / (3 * a) \<or>
            x = s3 - p / s3 - b / (3 * a))"

children.name: ccbrt
children.closed_by: its own proof: rcis_Ex gives the polar form z = rcis r a, the witness r' and a/3 are built so that rcis r' (a/3)^3 = rcis r a by (cases "r < 0") (simp_all add: DeMoivre2), giving EX w. w^3 = z, and someI_ex [OF *] closes it by unfolding ccbrt_def
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the cube-root witness: (ccbrt z)^3 = z for any complex z (the statement is copied by statements.py)

children.name: cubic_reduction
children.statement:
lemma cubic_reduction:
  fixes a :: complex
  assumes
    "a \<noteq> 0 \<and> x = y - b / (3 * a) \<and>  p = (3* a * c - b^2) / (9 * a^2) \<and>
      q = (9 * a * b * c - 2 * b^3 - 27 * a^2 * d) / (54 * a^3)"
  shows "a * x^3 + b * x^2 + c * x + d = 0 \<longleftrightarrow> y^3 + 3 * p * y - 2 * q = 0"
children.closed_by: by algebra: the three divisions in the assumptions are first turned into products with field_simps, then `from assms [unfolded *] show ?thesis by algebra`
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the reduction: a*x^3 + b*x^2 + c*x + d = 0 <-> y^3 + 3*p*y - 2*q = 0 under x = y - b/(3*a) and the definitions of p and q (the statement is copied by statements.py)

children.name: cubic_basic
children.statement:
lemma cubic_basic:
  fixes s :: complex
  assumes
    "s^2 = q^2 + p^3 \<and>
      s1^3 = (if p = 0 then 2 * q else q + s) \<and>
      s2 = -s1 * (1 + i * t) / 2 \<and>
      s3 = -s1 * (1 - i * t) / 2 \<and>
      i^2 + 1 = 0 \<and>
      t^2 = 3"
  shows
    "if p = 0
     then y^3 + 3 * p * y - 2 * q = 0 \<longleftrightarrow> y = s1 \<or> y = s2 \<or> y = s3
     else s1 \<noteq> 0 \<and>
      (y^3 + 3 * p * y - 2 * q = 0 \<longleftrightarrow> (y = s1 - p / s1 \<or> y = s2 - p / s2 \<or> y = s3 - p / s3))"
children.closed_by: a case split on p = 0; each branch closes by (simp add: field_simps) algebra, the False branch first deriving s1 /= 0, s2 /= 0, s3 /= 0 and the three rewrites y = si - p/si <-> si*y = si^2 - p
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the solution of the depressed form: y^3 + 3*p*y - 2*q = 0 <-> y = s1 | y = s2 | y = s3 (if p = 0) or the analogous y = si - p/si disjunction (if p /= 0) (the statement is copied by statements.py)

applicability.goal_shape: A closed-form solution of a general polynomial equation, stated as an equivalence poly(a,b,c,d,x) = 0 <-> x = r1 | x = r2 | x = r3 between the equation and a disjunction of explicit root expressions, over an algebraically closed coefficient type (complex here), with the roots given by a let-block of auxiliary expressions (p, q, s, s1, s2, s3).
applicability.use_when: the target equation reduces by an invertible change of variable to a normal form with a known, self-contained solution; the reduction is an iff (<->), so the transfer back is pure rewriting; the normal form's solution and the witness that makes it concrete can each be stated as their own lemma with no reference to the original goal.
applicability.avoid_when: the reduction is one-way (an implication, not an iff), so the normal form's solutions need not be the original's; the normal form's solution needs the original goal's hypotheses (so it cannot be stated separately); the transfer step itself is non-trivial and needs its own lemma.

consequences: Creates three obligations: the reduction equivalence (cubic_reduction), the witness (ccbrt), and the normal-form solution (cubic_basic); the glue then only has to instantiate and rewrite. The transfer depends on the reduction being an iff and on the branch condition p = 0 vs p /= 0 being expressed consistently in the normal-form lemma (there p = 0 directly) and in the glue (there re-expressed as a * (c * 3) = b^2); a mismatch between the two branch conditions breaks the final `cases` step. The witness ccbrt is defined with SOME, so the glue can use it only because the lemma ccbrt has already discharged its existence obligation; without that lemma the value of ccbrt is under-determined.
